description: The new country-wide District read materializes ineligible entities before filtering, with no page bound.

finding.failure_scenario: The new country-wide District read materializes ineligible entities before filtering, with no page bound.
finding.model_authored_prose: This new `crud.GetAll[models.District]` has no `.Limit()`, so it materializes every district in the country including the ineligible ones it then discards in memory — push the eligibility predicates into the query, or page it. Introduced by this change. Before this diff the district-side read was `crud.GetMulti[models.District]` over keys derived from the admin UDIs that had already been found (removed at old line 1753), so it was bounded by the admin-UDI set; now it is bounded only by how many District entities exist with that country_code, and the eligibility filter runs afterwards in memory at lines 1862-1874. District is a wide model (61 `datastore:` properties in services/districts/models/district.go) and the whole entity is loaded, not a projection. The predicates being filtered in memory are stored, indexable properties — `District.EligibleForKADEmails()` at services/districts/models/district.go:451 is just `SendKADEmails() && m.RosterSyncingEnabled` over `dont_send_kad_emails`/`roster_syncing_enabled`, and `IsTest` is `is_test` — so adding them as equality filters on the query (and the matching index.yaml entry), or paging with `.Limit()` plus a cursor and handling one page per invocation, would bound the read. I traced both callers (monthly_admin_email_batch.go:444 and kad_email_subscriptions.go:529) and neither is in a transaction and neither bounds the result before this point, so nothing upstream or downstream caps it.
finding.summary: This new `crud.GetAll[models.District]` has no `.Limit()`, so it materializes every district in the country including the ineligible ones it then discards in memory — push the eligibility predicates into the query, or page it.
